reason: The key premise that Gd micro-alloying significantly impacts glass-forming ability in P-containing alloys is directly supported by E3 and E4, which show a notable effect of 1 at% Gd on the Pd-Ni-P system. The baseline alloy's behavior (amorphous formation on rapid quenching, limited stability) is supported by E1. However, the mechanistic premise that Gd increases size mismatch and thus retards nucleation in this specific high-entropy alloy is not directly evidenced by the cited passages, which only model the Pd-Ni-P system and do not discuss the CrMnFeCoNiP composition.
premises: Gd addition increases atomic size mismatch and chemical heterogeneity in the alloy
Increased size/chemical mismatch kinetically retards crystal nucleation by raising the energy barrier
Gd micro-alloying significantly impacts glass-forming ability in P-containing alloys, unlike Co, Cu, Fe
